patterns.comment: A doc comment opens `/**`. `/**/` is an empty block comment and not the opening of one, which the lookahead keeps.
patterns.name: comment.block.documentation.sysl

nestedComment.comment: A block comment nests: `/*` inside one opens another, which needs its own `*/`. The rule includes itself, so each `*/` closes the innermost comment still open and the text after the outermost one is code again.
nestedComment.name: comment.block.sysl

docTag.comment: A tag is `@name` at the start of a line of a doc comment, after an optional `*` margin, and only from the closed vocabulary; any other `@name` is prose.

patterns.comment: A backtick-quoted identifier is a NAME, so it is scoped as a variable rather than as a string — a reader should see `match` as the name it is and not as text. It sits above every other rule because what is inside it is a name whatever it looks like: a reserved word, an operator, a quote.
patterns.name: variable.other.quoted.sysl

string.comment: Every quote form, tripled first: a text block opens `"""` and the one-line form would otherwise read its first two quotes as an empty string. A prefix says how a literal is read and the quote form how it is written, so each prefix has both. Only `s` and `f` read holes; only `raw` decodes no escapes.

patterns.comment: A raw block decodes no escapes and reads no holes, so nothing joins its lines either.
patterns.name: string.quoted.triple.raw.sysl

patterns.comment: A lone `"` inside a block is ordinary text; `\"` is stepped over whole, so `\"""` does not close it.
patterns.name: string.quoted.triple.sysl

patterns.comment: A one-line raw string ends at its first `"`: there is no escape.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.raw.sysl

hole.comment: `$$` is one literal dollar; `${expr}` holds any expression; `$name` is the short form.

holeWithSpec.comment: An f-string's hole, which may be followed by a printf specifier: flags, width, precision and one conversion letter of the closed set.

escape.comment: The nine named escapes — C's set, with no `\e`, `\a` or `\v` — and the braced `\u{H…}` of one to six hex digits. Anything else after a backslash is refused by the lexer.

lineJoin.comment: In a text block a `\` at the end of a line joins it to the next.
lineJoin.name: constant.character.escape.line-continuation.sysl

char.comment: A char literal is one Unicode scalar value, or one escape, between single quotes.
char.name: string.quoted.single.sysl

label.comment: A loop label, `'name`: told from a char literal by the absence of a closing quote.
label.name: entity.name.label.sysl

number.comment: A suffix names a canonical primitive: `iN` / `uN` / `fN` of any width, `usize`, `isize`, `bf16`, or a fixed-point `iWqF` / `uWqF`. The prefix letter may be either case; `_` groups digits. Hex digits include `f`, so a hex integer cannot carry a float suffix and a hex float needs its `p` exponent.

patterns.comment: A `.` is part of a number only with a digit after it, so `0..<n` and `1.max()` stay what they are. A fraction may carry a float or a fixed-point suffix.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.sysl

patterns.comment: A whole number with a float suffix is a float, as the lexer reads it: `3f16`.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.sysl

attribute.comment: An annotation above a declaration (@test, @test(should_trap), @tailrec) and a directive at the margin (#if). Two sigils because they are two kinds of thing; a pattern's infix '@' is not matched here, since this anchors to the start of a line.

patterns.comment: struct / enum / trait / impl / module, and the name each one introduces. A letter is Unicode's letter, as it is in the lexer, and a combining mark continues a name the way a letter does.
`end` is contextual: a block's closing marker only when it stands alone on its line or names the block it closes, so `end = 3` and `end.max()` read it as the ordinary name it is there.
A function declaration: a name at the head of a line, after its modifiers, then a parameter list. A control word is never the name, so `while (x)` and `match (a, b)` stay keywords.

declModifier.comment: `set` (a setter) and `async`, read only inside a declaration's run of modifiers, where they cannot be anything else; elsewhere `set` is an ordinary name.
declModifier.name: storage.modifier.sysl

patterns.comment: Reserved words that steer control flow, and the contextual `become`.
patterns.name: keyword.control.sysl

patterns.comment: `await` is a keyword only where an operand follows it.
patterns.name: keyword.control.sysl

patterns.comment: The `c` of a `c const` or `c type` block, which is special only before one of those two words.
Reserved words that bind or declare. `ref` is here rather than with the modifiers because it is a declaration and never a type — there is no `ref T` to qualify.
patterns.name: keyword.declaration.sysl

patterns.comment: Modifiers and the contract vocabulary. The capability words are deliberately absent: they are annotations now (@no_alloc, @requires(...)), styled by the annotation rule above, and 'alloc', 'no' and 'requires' are ordinary identifiers a program may use for its own. `async` is one only where a declaration follows it.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.sysl

patterns.comment: Soft keywords — special only where the grammar expects one, an ordinary identifier elsewhere.
patterns.name: keyword.other.sysl

patterns.comment: Compile-time operators over a type.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.word.sysl

patterns.comment: Predeclared scalars. These are identifiers the analyzer resolves, not reserved words, which is what lets the open iN / uN / fN families need no lexical support. Only the usual widths are matched, since `f1` and `i2` are as often a program's own names; fixed point's iWqF / uWqF and q7 / q15 / q31 are matched by shape.
patterns.name: support.type.primitive.sysl

patterns.comment: A capitalised name is a type by convention. The convention is about CASE, so a script that has none -- CJK, Hebrew, Arabic -- gets neither this nor the call rule below, which is the honest answer rather than a guess. The boundaries are written out rather than as \b so that the word set this rule reads is stated here rather than inherited from whatever engine renders the grammar.
patterns.name: entity.name.type.sysl

patterns.comment: A reserved identifier. The __NAME__ *shape* belongs to the language, so the shape is what is matched rather than the built-ins that currently occupy it — a later release adding one needs no change here.
patterns.name: constant.language.builtin.sysl

call.comment: A name applied to arguments, after declarations have had their chance at the line.

operator.comment: Only the memory-mode sigils and the assignments that yield are scoped, and deliberately so. Which of `T` / `&T` / `*T` a type is in is the thing a reader of sysl most needs to see, and a renderer that also colours every `=` and `+` buries it. `:=` and `+:=` … `>>:=` are expressions with a value, which is worth seeing where they sit inside a condition; each is one token, as the lexer reads it. Arithmetic and comparison are left to the body colour.
